# Phase One — Boundless Geelooy Revival Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos makes each pixel possible anew; Awtsmoos.com can therefore reveal simplicity without becoming plain.
The ideal is not fewer capabilities, but capabilities arranged so intention arrives before ornament and function before strain.

## North Star

Imagine every public surface behaving like one coherent civilization: a user knows where they are, what matters now, what action comes next, what succeeded, and how to recover when it fails.

## Unlimited Possibilities

1. A global route health map that discovers every public entry and records runtime, layout, interaction, accessibility, and performance signals.
2. A public quality dashboard that groups pages by healthy, degraded, broken, blocked-by-auth, and intentional-tooling status.
3. A shared shell vocabulary for headers, back navigation, page title, primary action, contextual rail, status, empty state, and mobile drawer.
4. A universal progressive-disclosure contract: advanced controls stay available but do not compete with the primary task.
5. A density budget per viewport so pages cannot silently accumulate five simultaneous panels.
6. A visual hierarchy budget that limits equal-weight headings, borders, glows, pills, and competing accent colors.
7. A responsive contract that guarantees one-column task flow at phone width unless the task genuinely requires a canvas.
8. A game acceptance harness that verifies start, movement/input, objective progress, restart/recovery, HUD legibility, and win/fail transitions.
9. A canvas/app acceptance harness that distinguishes an intentionally blank work area from a failed render.
10. A browser journey library that can exercise search, social publishing, editors, games, media, login, and navigation with reusable primitives.
11. Route screenshots at canonical desktop, phone, and short-height sizes for human comparison.
12. DOM measurements for overflow, touch targets, unnamed controls, hidden focus, excessive fixed layers, and empty canvases.
13. Performance budgets for route load, long tasks, animation pressure, and oversized asset waterfalls.
14. Shared motion tokens that disable ornamental movement under reduced-motion without breaking feedback.
15. Shared spacing/type tokens that reduce the tendency for every feature to invent a new visual language.
16. Page-local CSS ownership so a repair does not destabilize unrelated routes.
17. Explicit state styling for loading, error, empty, success, disabled, selected, active, hover, focus-visible, and offline states.
18. Game-specific onboarding overlays that teach controls only until the player demonstrates competence.
19. Game HUDs that hide secondary metrics until context makes them useful.
20. Editor workspaces that reserve the largest visual region for content rather than tool chrome.
21. Search surfaces that foreground query + results and move libraries/history/help into optional context.
22. Social creation that uses a guided progression instead of displaying every destination and content type at once.
23. A route registry generated from real files but curated with semantics: public, dynamic, fixture, template, legacy, internal tool, and experimental.
24. A route-debt ledger linking every broken symptom to owning files, test evidence, and completion proof.
25. A concurrency-aware repair scheduler that avoids routes currently owned by active agents.
26. A shared “clear task” design review rule: one primary action, one obvious status, one dominant content region.
27. Automated checks that prohibit accidental horizontal overflow and unreachable fixed controls.
28. A game input abstraction that tests keyboard, pointer, and touch paths where each game claims support.
29. A public index audit so working apps/games are discoverable and dead ones are not promoted as finished.
30. A graceful experimental badge/status model for unfinished experiences instead of pretending every prototype is production-ready.

## Five Competing Architectures

### A — Global Redesign Layer
Apply one universal stylesheet and shell across every route. Fast visual convergence, but dangerously invasive and likely to create cascade regressions.

### B — Route-by-Route Reconstruction
Repair each route locally with strict ownership. Safest behaviorally, but risks visual drift and duplicated solutions.

### C — Shared Contracts + Local Skins
Define small cross-site contracts for hierarchy, responsiveness, states, and accessibility while keeping route-local CSS/components. Strong balance of coherence and containment.

### D — Runtime-Gate First
Build quality tooling and change only routes that fail measurable gates. Excellent evidence discipline, but subjective clutter can survive if metrics are too narrow.

### E — Journey-First Product Repair
Select representative user journeys, repair them end-to-end, then expand by category. Strong user value, but route coverage can lag.

## Preferred Synthesis

Use C + D + E: shared quality contracts, measured runtime gates, and end-to-end journey reconstruction. Avoid a giant global visual override. The Awtsmoos can be one without making every vessel identical; coherence should come from principles, not one monolithic stylesheet.

## First Safe Journey

`/mawgawl/sefarim/` is the first implementation candidate because its source tree is clean while screenshot-adjacent game/social/app surfaces are under active modification.

## NEXT_ACTION

Map theoretical files and responsibilities for the Sefarim reconstruction plus the sitewide audit path, then critique this phase before any production code is changed.
